title: Your UDID Card and What It Unlocks

level-1.title: A card that helps
summary: There is a special card for Deaf and hard-of-hearing people in India. It is called a UDID card.
It shows, anywhere in India, that you are Deaf. You do not have to explain again and again.
The card helps your family get money for school books, hearing aids and travel.
It is free to ask for one. A trusted adult and a government doctor help you get it.
Ask a grown-up at home if you have a UDID card. Many families do not know about it.

questions.prompt: What does the UDID card show?

image.alt: An identity card with a shield on it

options.label: That you are Deaf, anywhere in India
How much money you have
Which shop you like

questions.hint: It is an identity card, not a money card.

questions.prompt: How much does it cost to ask for a UDID card?

options.label: Nothing. It is free.

questions.hint: Anyone asking you to pay for it is not telling the truth.

questions.prompt: Who helps you get the card?

image.alt: An adult and a child at a counter

options.label: A trusted adult and a government doctor
A stranger who messages your phone
Nobody, you do it in secret

questions.hint: A stranger messaging about money or cards is a warning sign.

level-2.title: The card, the hearing aid and the pension
summary: The UDID card is the gateway. Almost every other scheme asks for it first, so nothing else starts until you have one.
To get it you need a disability certificate from a government medical board, usually showing 40% or more — what the law calls a benchmark disability.
ADIP is the scheme that pays for equipment: hearing aids, and cochlear implants for people who qualify. It depends on family income and is run through government hospitals, ALIMCO and approved NGOs.
Most states pay a monthly disability pension. The amount is different in every state, and usually needs 40% disability plus income and residence rules.
For families below the poverty line there is also a central pension, IGNDPS, which some states top up.
Travel costs less too — Indian Railways and many state buses give concessions to disabled passengers.
None of this arrives on its own. Somebody has to apply. That is the single most useful thing in this lesson.

questions.prompt: Why is the UDID card called a gateway?

image.alt: A gate with several paths behind it

options.label: Most other schemes ask for it before anything else
It works as a bank card
It is only for travel

questions.hint: Think about what has to happen first.

questions.prompt: Which scheme pays for a hearing aid?

image.alt: A hearing aid in a case

options.label: ADIP
IGNDPS
Post-Matric Scholarship

questions.hint: ADIP is the scheme for aids and appliances — equipment, not cash.

questions.prompt: Your family has never applied for anything. What is true about the pension and the schemes?

options.label: They are not automatic. Somebody must apply.
They arrive by themselves when you turn 18
The school applies for every child

questions.hint: This is why so much of this money goes unclaimed.

level-3.title: Claiming it: tax, health and the paperwork
summary: Section 80U lets a person with a disability take a flat deduction from taxable income — ₹75,000 at 40–79%, and ₹1,25,000 where the disability is severe. It needs no bills or receipts.
Section 80DD does the same for a family member supporting a dependant with a disability. One household usually claims one or the other, not both for the same person.
Over a working life these deductions are worth a large sum, and they are among the most commonly missed.
Health cover: eligible families may come under Ayushman Bharat or a state health scheme, which pays for hospital treatment.

Some support is routed through National Trust registered organisations — caregiver help, community living, rehabilitation — but eligibility depends on which disability category applies, so check before relying on it.
Everything above is a right attached to paperwork. The order is: disability certificate, then UDID, then each scheme separately.
Rules, amounts and income limits change. Confirm the current position on the official portal or with the district social welfare office before you count on a figure.
None of this is charity. It exists because being Deaf costs money that hearing people never have to spend.

questions.prompt: Under Section 80U, what does a person with a 50% disability deduct from taxable income?

image.alt: A tax form with a line filled in

options.label: Nothing

questions.hint: ₹1,25,000 is the higher figure, for severe disability.

questions.prompt: Do you need receipts to claim the Section 80U deduction?

image.alt: A pile of bills beside a form

options.label: No. It is a flat deduction.
Yes, every medical bill
Yes, bills plus a doctor's letter each month

questions.hint: It does not depend on what you actually spent.

options.label: Disability certificate, then UDID, then each scheme
Apply for schemes first, get the card later
Any order works

questions.hint: Each step is the paperwork the next one asks for.
